question.text: For NRI clients investing through PMS:

answer.text: PIS approval is not required for PMS investments; NRI PMS clients use NRE/NRO designated bank accounts with RBI-approved PMS providers under SEBI PMS Regulations
A PIS account under the RBI framework is mandatory for PMS investments
No regulatory framework applies to NRI PMS investments
Only a demat account is enough, with no banking arrangement required

explanation.text: The Logic: The Portfolio Investment Scheme (PIS) is an RBI facility for NRIs/OCIs and is needed for direct stock trading. For PMS investments, however, PIS approval is not required. NRI PMS clients instead operate through NRE/NRO designated bank accounts with RBI-approved PMS providers under SEBI's PMS Regulations. The Trap: Assuming PIS applies to every NRI investment route conflates direct equity trading with the PMS route. PMS sits outside the PIS requirement. Note: Tie the answer to the NRE/NRO designated bank account plus RBI-approved PMS provider combination cited in the source rather than to PIS.
